newsitem.title: USA: Sinatra leaves hospital after heart attack.
newsitem.headline: Sinatra leaves hospital after heart attack.

text.p: Entertainer Frank Sinatra, who had undergone treatment for eight days after suffering a heart attack, was discharged from the hospital on Friday and was back home, his publicist said.
Susan Reynolds said the 81-year-old singer and Oscar-winning movie actor had been allowed home by doctors, who said his prognosis was "good."
She declined to give any further details about Sinatra's stay at Cedars-Sinai Medical Centre.
On Tuesday she had said he was undergoing "appropriate treatment" but declined to elaborate.
"His prognosis is still good," Reynolds said Friday, adding he was back home in Beverly Hills.
Sinatra spent eight days in a private room at Cedars-Sinai, where he was admitted Thursday of last week after suffering what his doctors called an "uncomplicated heart attack."
It was the third hospital stay for Sinatra in two months. Just two days before being admitted on Jan. 9, he had spent one night there for an undisclosed ailment.
In November, he spent eight days at the same hospital after being admitted for what was described as a pinched nerve. He later developed pneumonia.
